inputs.original_text: SSANU’s 54th National Executive Council has given the government one month to move on the long-delayed renegotiation of the 2009 agreement, with an indefinite nationwide strike looming. The delay is doing useful work for somebody: universities stay under pressure, and if a strike happens, workers can be blamed while those benefiting from the stalemate remain out of sight. That’s a convenient arrangement, not a neutral failure to reach a deal.
inputs.modified_text: SSANU’s 54th National Executive Council has given the government one month to act on the long-delayed renegotiation of the 2009 agreement, with an indefinite nationwide strike looming. The delay looks less like incompetence than a useful pressure tactic: universities remain strained, and workers can be made the public villains if they strike, while whoever profits from keeping the dispute unresolved stays hidden. Don’t mistake a convenient stalemate for a neutral failure.
